breadcrumb: 21. Portland Metro Chamber — Tax Reform & Regional Economy Letter
tldr: The Portland Metro Chamber submits a March 31, 2026 letter asserting Oregon faces structural economic crisis, citing regional recession since 2023, poor consumer sentiment, housing constraints, and record office vacancy. The Chamber urges six urgent priorities: tax reform by December 31, 2029 (before SALT deduction relief expires), restore traded-sector competitiveness, unlock housing production, rebuild economic value proposition, modernize regulatory systems, and strengthen talent pipelines. They emphasize Oregon's highest marginal income tax rate and vulnerability to federal tax policy changes.

bullets.text: Portland region has been in localized recession since 2023
Portland's commercial office vacancies are highest in modern history and one of highest in nation
Portland region 80 out of 81 on real estate invest-ability
Nearly last multifamily housing permitting in nation; 60% of regional permitting activity in SW Washington
Loss of approximately $3 billion in taxable income from Multnomah County
Oregon has highest marginal tax rate in nation and only county in America with four income taxes
SALT deduction temporary relief (HB1, enacted 2025) will expire December 31, 2029
Tax reform must be enacted for effective date of no later than January 1, 2030
At current pace, additional decade needed to fully recover from pandemic impacts on downtown office foot traffic
